_note: Field-move obstacles (bible §7 'Field moves'): each needs one friend's field move; the others can't clear it, so the player SWITCHes. Kept apart from the map files (the World track owns those): map + tile. 'art' is a prop from art/locations/out/graded (drawn on the tile). 'reward' is found when it's cleared. Kinds and their lines are in 'kinds'. Optional: 'sprite'/'dir'/'leaves' (a person in the way), 'replaces' (stands in for a map piece with that art, e.g. the broken bridge), 'onObject' (no picture: it is the object on the tile), 'blockedTalk'/'clearTalk' (dialogue ids said instead of 'blocked' and after clearing). Route 1 order: Nolan's bridge opens the east bank, Haydon's officer guards the stairs down to the checkpoint, Callum's stone is on the west cliff. Positions are first guesses; move them when maps change. Chapter 1's storm quest on Route 1's west hill: Callum scans the storm-rod's plate (r1_rod_plate, sights Wardeye), Haydon taunts the clerk off the Cloud Clamp (r1_clerk), then Nolan unsplices the rod's cable from the Clamp (r1_clamp: 'after' both, sets storm_returned, plays the storm). Dani's rock by the rod hides the second Storm Shard.

boulder.blocked: A boulder blocks the way. It won't budge.
boulder.hint: Dani could shift this with the Shield.
boulder.clear: Dani put a shoulder into it. The boulder rolled clear!

guard.blocked: A Tally officer won't let anyone past.
guard.hint: Haydon could bait him off his post.
guard.clear: The officer stormed off after Haydon. The way is clear!

broken.clear: Nolan patched it with his cable. It works!

sealed.blocked: Old Relic writing covers it. Nobody can read it.
sealed.hint: Callum could Scan this and read it.
sealed.clear: Callum scanned the writing. It opened!
sealed.shout: Hold on, I've seen this font.

obstacles.clearLine: Callum scanned the plate. The keepers' writing lit up, one rune at a time.
The clerk stormed off after Haydon, waving Form 12-R. The Clamp is unguarded!
Nolan pulled the Tally's cable off the rod and patched the rod back into the ground line.
